title: eng-oncall
text:
eng-oncall

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager fired: PD-INC-91234 (synthetic-canary-errors)

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert triggered by service: router-proxy (severity: P3) — incident link: https://pagerduty.example/INCIDENTS/91234

maria: seeing the page, checking dashboards now. any customer reports?

tilly: i have a small uptick in 5xx on eu-west canaries, looks synthetic. digging now — starting with canary cluster health.

kevin: FYI alert rule: `synthetic_canary_errors > 5 for 3m` — we recently made that change to be more sensitive.

sam: no external tickets in Intercom, prod-telemetry shows a 0.2% spike in 5xx across a handful of routes, mostly canaries.

maria: nice — likely noisy. can we confirm origin? e.g., deployment/canary job or a transient infra blip?

tilly: logs show repeated 502 from router-proxy to model-backend from a particular host pool `canary-az-b-3` around 1739502400. tailing logs now:

tilly: ```
2024-06-24T18:06:32Z router-proxy[pid=4521] WARN upstream 502 host=10.12.5.23 backend=model-backend-c1
2024-06-24T18:06:33Z router-proxy[pid=4521] WARN upstream 502 host=10.12.5.23 backend=model-backend-c1
2024-06-24T18:06:34Z router-proxy[pid=4521] INFO connection reset timeout
```

maria: that host looks like a canary instance. did any canary deployment run at ~18:05?

kevin: deployment webhook shows `canary/seed-20240624` started at 18:04, but rollout was quick and succeeded. Possibly brief port restart on that host.

incident-bot: Pager acknowledged by maria at 1739502462

maria: acked and watching, i'm going to cordon the host from canary rotation to see if errors drop.

tilly: removed 10.12.5.23 from canary pool, traffic draining. watching metrics.

sam: metrics trending back down — canary errors back to baseline in last minute.

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD-INC-91234 auto-resolved (no responders escalated).

maria: marking no customer impact. only synthetic traffic and canary pool misbehavior. recommend we mute the synthetic rule during canary rollouts or increase threshold.

kevin: +1 to changing the rule. current threshold triggers during normal canary churn. Maybe change to `> 10 for 5m` or add tag-based suppression when deployment flag `canary_in_progress=true`

tilly: filing a small follow-up: infra ticket to add a drain/retry backoff to canary agent so we don't generate repeated 502s on host restarts. Also adding PD suppression play for `deployment:canary`.

maria: quick postmortem notes:
- cause: brief canary host restart produced transient 502s to model-backend
- impact: synthetic-only, no customer-facing errors observed
- mitigation: cordoned host, drained traffic, errors recovered within ~90s
- follow-ups: adjust synthetic alert thresholds OR add canary suppression; implement canary agent backoff; add a short runbook blurb for oncall to check deploy webhooks before paging.

sam: can you add the screenshots/links to the incident in the follow-up ticket? i'll attach graphs.

maria: will do. closing thread now. :white_check_mark:

tilly: thanks — handing back to normal rotation.

kevin: noted for the next eng-standup, might be worth a 5-min heads-up to SRE and platform teams.

incident-bot: Thread closed by maria at 1739502830
